## 9.1 What the OS does for a game

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A game never talks to the hardware alone, because it asks the operating system.
- The OS runs processes, shares memory, keeps files and controls devices.
- The OS also checks permissions, for example for the camera.
- **Do it:** Open Settings › About on the lab computer and on your phone. Which OS and version does each have?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/os-layers.png)
:::
::::

## Example · The player taps the game icon

The player taps the icon of Pocket Quest on the phone.
**Which services of the OS work now?**

::: {.reveal}
1. Files: the OS loads the game from storage into RAM.
2. Processes and memory: the OS starts a process and gives it its own RAM.
3. Devices: the OS sends every tap to the game and shows its frames.
:::

## Try it 1 · OS services

a) The game asks to use the camera. Which service of the OS decides?
b) The game saves the progress to storage. Which service does it use?
c) A tap on the screen reaches the game. Which service brings it?

::: {.answer}
a) permissions
b) files
c) devices
:::

## 9.2 Processes and the scheduler

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A process is a running program with its own memory.
- The scheduler gives each process a time slice of a few ms on a core.
- A process is running, ready or waiting.
- **Do it:** Open Task Manager with Ctrl + Shift + Esc. Which three processes use the most memory?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/time-slices.png)
:::
::::

{{< sim file="sims/scheduler-lab.html" poster="sims/scheduler-lab.png" title="Scheduler Lab: one core, many processes" task="**Show:** open Download and Chat sync, then let the game load a file. **Ask:** why does the game get no slices while it waits?" >}}

## Try it 2 · Processes

a) The game waits for a level file from storage. What is its state?
b) All cores are busy, but the game could run. What is its state?
c) One core has slices of 4 ms, and the game and three other apps are ready. How long does the game run in every 16 ms?

::: {.answer}
a) waiting
b) ready
c) 4 ms
:::

## 9.3 Sharing the RAM

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The OS gives each process its own part of the RAM.
- When the RAM of a phone is full, the OS closes background apps.
- When the RAM of a PC is full, Windows uses the slow page file on the drive.
- **Do it:** In Task Manager › Performance › Memory, how much RAM is in use?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/ram-full.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Pocket Quest and the camera

A phone has 4 GB of RAM. The OS uses 1.5 GB, Pocket Quest 1.8 GB, and the camera needs 0.9 GB.
**What does the OS do when the player opens the camera?**

::: {.reveal}
1. In use before: 1.5 + 1.8 = 3.3 GB, so 0.7 GB is free.
2. With the camera: 3.3 + 0.9 = 4.2 GB, which is more than 4 GB.
3. The OS closes **Pocket Quest** in the background, and the camera keeps running.
:::

## Try it 3 · Memory

a) A phone has 6 GB. The OS uses 2 GB and a game 2.5 GB. How much RAM is free?
b) What does Windows do when the RAM is full?
c) What should a mobile game do when it goes to the background?

::: {.answer}
a) 1.5 GB
b) It uses the page file on the drive.
c) It should save its state.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/ram-rush.html" poster="sims/ram-rush.png" title="RAM Rush: you are the operating system of a phone" kind="game" task="**The story:** Pocket Quest runs on a 4 GB phone next to the camera, Chat and Music. **Play:** you are the OS; in each round, decide what fits and which app must close." >}}

## Try it 4 · The big level (harder)

The facts: the phone has 4 GB of RAM. The OS uses 1.5 GB and Pocket Quest 2.3 GB. Chat (0.4 GB) was used 1 minute ago, and Music (0.3 GB) 20 minutes ago.

a) How much RAM do all four need together?
b) Which app does the OS close first, and why?
c) Which apps must the OS close in the end?

::: {.answer}
a) 4.5 GB
b) Music, because it was used longest ago.
c) Music and Chat
:::

## Summary

- The OS manages the hardware and gives services to all apps.
- The scheduler shares the CPU cores between processes in short time slices.
- A process is running, ready or waiting.
- The OS gives each process its own part of the RAM.
- A full RAM makes a phone close background apps and a PC use the slow page file.
